edits.old: A search of the World Bank projects API for Uganda with oil palm, Kalangala or vegetable oil returns nothing. The case still carries a World Bank lender key, which is under review.
edits.new: A search of the World Bank projects API for Uganda with oil palm, Kalangala or vegetable oil returns nothing. The two sides also differ on why the Bank left: the IFAD evaluation says it "was concerned about compliance with its internal environmental safeguards policies" (para. 46), while Friends of the Earth International's 2012 report Land, life and justice says it feared the expanded project "would not comply with its internal forestry safeguard policies". The money Friends of the Earth attributes to the Bank is not Bank money in the ordinary sense either: its report gives "US$10 million from the World Bank through its private sector lending arm, the International Finance Corporation", against US$19.9 million from IFAD. Klaus Deininger of the Bank's Development Research Group denied to the Bretton Woods Project in 2012 that the Bank Group and the IFC were involved in the project. The IFC does have a documented connection, though a later one: the CAO registered a complaint on 13 January 2017 from the National Association of Professional Environmentalists on behalf of Bugala farmers, under IFC project 33385 with Bidco Africa Limited, over deforestation, compensation for expropriated land and lost livelihoods at the Kalangala operations of Bidco Uganda and Oil Palm Uganda Limited. The parties reached an agreement in August 2017, kept confidential at their request, and the CAO closed the case in 2018 after monitoring it.
